title: Et HaOchel
versionTitle: Akiva Publishing interlinear edition with translated source footnotes

p: בְּעִנְיְנֵי הָאֲכִילָה קִצּוּר קֻנְטְרֵס "עֵת הָאֹכֶל" מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ:
Concerning matters of eating; an abridgment of the treatise Et HaOchel from his holy handwriting:
הַפְּרִישׁוּת מֵאֲכִילָה נִקְרָא קְדוּשָׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּתַעֲנִית: הַיּוֹשֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית נִקְרָא קָדוֹשׁ;
Abstinence from food is termed sanctity, as it is written in the first chapter of Ta'anit [11a]: "One who sits in fasting is called holy";
וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "'וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם' — אֵלּוּ מַיִם רִאשׁוֹנִים, 'וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים' — אֵלּוּ מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים, 'כִּי אֲנִי ה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם' — זֶה שֶׁמֶן."

and they said (Berakhot 53b): "'And you shall sanctify yourselves'—this refers to the initial waters [washing before a meal]; 'and you shall be holy'—this refers to the final waters [washing after a meal]; 'for I am Hashem your God'—this refers to [anointing] oil."

פֵּרוּשׁ: מַיִם רִאשׁוֹנִים — רְחִיצַת הַיָּדַיִם שֶׁהֵם כְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מְיֻחָס לַיָּדַיִם, יִהְיוּ מְנֻקִּים מִכָּל לִכְלוּךְ וְגִיעוּל שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה חִיצוֹנִית, בִּלְתִּי וְרַק לַה' לְבַדּוֹ, לְהַחֲיוֹת גּוּפוֹ לִרְצוֹן ה'.

Meaning: the initial waters refer to the washing of the hands, which are the instruments of action, since in every context action is attributed to the hands; that they should be cleansed from all filth and revulsion of external lust, focused purely and exclusively upon Hashem alone to sustain one's body in accordance with Hashem's will.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הָרְחִיצָה בַּמַּיִם — מֵי הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "בָּרָאתִי תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין",
And this is achieved through washing with water—the waters of divine knowledge, which is the Torah, as it is written: "I created the Torah as an antidote-spice,"

שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע רֹאשׁ תַּאֲוָתוֹ שֶׁבַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "כִּי יֵצֶר לֶב [הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו]" וְגוֹמֵר, וְתַאֲוָה מְיֻחֶסֶת בְּכָל מָקוֹם לַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "לֵב חוֹמֵד".

for the evil inclination is always rooted in the desires of the heart, as written: "for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth," and lust is everywhere ascribed to the heart, as stated: "the heart covets."

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁרַק הַהַתְחָלָה מֵהָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "פִּתְחוּ לִי וְכוּלֵי וַאֲנִי אֶפְתַּח וְכוּלֵי",

Nevertheless, our Sages of blessed memory taught: "Were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, assists him, etc.," for only the initial opening begins with man, as written: "Open for Me an opening... and I will open for you...";
כְּעִנְיַן בַּקָּשַׁת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיכֶם", שֶׁתַּשְׁלוּם שְׁלֵמוּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹזְרוֹ.

reflecting the prayer of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him: "May it be the divine will that the Shechinah rest upon the work of your hands," for the completion and perfection of the action is granted when the Blessed Name assists him.
וְזֶהוּ "וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים" — אֵלּוּ מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים, שֶׁאַחַר אֲכִילָה רוֹחֵץ יָדָיו, שֶׁגַּם כֵּן הֵם מְנֻקִּים מִשּׁוּם טִנּוּפֶת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
And this is "and you shall be holy"—referring to the final waters, where after eating he washes his hands, which are likewise cleansed from all spiritual grime of this world.
וּכְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּיוֹמָא עַל "וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם וְכוּלֵי": אָדָם מְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ מְעַט — מְקַדְּשִׁין אוֹתוֹ הַרְבֵּה וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי.
And as our Sages expounded in Yoma [39a] on "and you shall sanctify yourselves": a person sanctifies himself a little—they sanctify him greatly from above, etc.; see there, and as I have written.
וּלְכָךְ מַיִם רִאשׁוֹנִים מִצְוָה, שֶׁהַמִּצְוֹת הֵם סְגֻלַּת הָאָדָם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא "וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם", וּלְכָךְ מְבָרֵךְ "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ";

Therefore the initial washing is a mitzvah, for the commandments are man's unique treasure through which "and you shall sanctify yourselves" is initiated, which is why one recites the blessing "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us";
וּמַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים חוֹבָה, שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַדְּשׁוֹ כְּחוֹב שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִפָּטֵר.
while the final waters are an obligation (chovah), for the Holy One sanctifies him from above as an absolute duty from which one cannot be exempt.
וְשֶׁמֶן, הָרוֹמֵז לְחָכְמָה שֶׁהִיא הַיְּדִיעָה וְהַכָּרָה הַבְּרוּרָה שֶׁ"אֲנִי אֱלֹהֵיכֶם",
And oil hints at Wisdom (Chochmah), which is the clear knowledge and recognition that "I am your God";
זֶה בָּא אַחַר הָאֲכִילָה הַהֲגוּנָה כָּרָאוּי לְשֵׁם ה', כְּדֵי לְהַחֲיוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ, אָז מוֹסֶפֶת לוֹ חָכְמָה וְדַעַת ה' אַחַר כָּךְ;
this descends after proper, sanctified eating undertaken for the sake of Hashem's Name solely to sustain life, imparting to him increased wisdom and knowledge of Hashem thereafter;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֲכִילָה גַּסָּה כִּבְהֵמָה מְטַמְטֶמֶת הַלֵּב וְהַמֹּחַ,
whereas gross, animalistic indulgence dulls and obstructs both the heart and the brain,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא קַמָּא ע״ב עַמּוּד א׳): "הַאי דְּלָא אֲמָרִי לָךְ וְכוּלֵי — דְּלָא אֲכַלִי בִּשְׂרָא דְּתוֹרָא".
just as the Talmud states (Bava Kamma 72a): "The reason I did not tell you this earlier... was because I had not yet eaten beef."

paragraphs.text: Taanit 11a:14-17: “Shmuel said: Whoever undertakes a fast is called a sinner. He follows Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, who asked: Why does Scripture say of the nazirite, ‘He shall atone for him for having sinned against the soul’? Against whose soul did he sin? He afflicted himself by abstaining from wine. If one who abstained from wine alone is called a sinner, how much more one who abstains from everything. Rabbi Elazar says: He is called holy, as it says, ‘He shall be holy; he shall let the hair of his head grow.’ If one who abstained from only one thing is called holy, how much more one who abstains from everything.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 68: “All the services performed through the bodily limbs and their mitzvot are only to straighten the heart; the heart is the essential point, for there is the dwelling of Hashem. These are the things that bring one to the goal. ‘After the wind, a tumult—but Hashem was not in the tumult ... a still, thin voice.’ The glory of Hashem is not in what is outwardly felt and tumultuous, but in the still, thin voice, the heart hidden from every creature. Yet first there must be force and tumult against the inclination, as the Sages said, ‘A person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination.’ This is not yet complete mastery; that comes when it is without tumult, as David said, ‘My heart is emptied within me.’”

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 31: “On Yom Kippur a person rises beyond the garments and receives the support of his existence from the inward voice, the utterance of Hashem, without a garment. He consequently recognizes that all the garments he possessed before also existed only through that divine utterance which gives them life. Since those garments did not conceal the inward voice from him, but enabled him to reach it and leave them behind, this itself proves that the food and drink he had on the ninth contained the divine name within them: ‘A person does not live by bread alone, but by every utterance of Hashem.’ Therefore one who eats and drinks on the ninth is counted as having fasted on both days: through the fast of the tenth, the divine utterance in the preceding eating and drinking becomes known to him.”

A transgression draws another transgression of its own corresponding kind. Therefore, ‘Do not become intoxicated’ through the appetite for eating, ‘and you will not sin’ through the appetite for forbidden relations. p: וְתִקּוּן תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה קוֹדֶמֶת אֶל הָאָדָם, שֶׁהִיא הַקַּלָּה גַּם כֵּן קְצָת אֶצְלוֹ, וּמִמֶּנָּה יִמָּשֵׁךְ אֶל תִּקּוּן תַּאֲוָה הַשְּׁנִיָּה;
And rectifying the desire for food must precede in man, being somewhat lighter for him to master, through which he is led toward rectifying the second desire;
וּלְכָךְ הִקְדִּימוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מַסֶּכֶת נָזִיר לְמַסֶּכֶת סוֹטָה,
which is why our Sages placed Tractate Nazir before Tractate Sotah [in the ordering of Seder Nashim],
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּצַּד הַשְּׁלֵמוּת, שְׁלֵמוּת בַּתַּאֲוָה הַשְּׁנִיָּה הוּא בְּמַעֲלָה יוֹתֵר,
even though from the standpoint of ultimate perfection, conquering the second lust is far more elevated,
שֶׁכֵּן עָנְשָׁהּ גַּם כֵּן יַתִּיר, מִסְּתָמָא גַּם מַעֲלַת תִּקּוּנָהּ עָצוּם,
its punishment being far more severe, indicating that the virtue of its rectification is immense,
וּלְכָךְ בַּתּוֹרָה קָדְמָה פָּרָשַׁת סוֹטָה לְפָרָשַׁת נָזִיר כְּפִי הַמַּעֲלָה;
which is why in the Written Torah the passage of Sotah precedes the passage of the Nazirite in accordance with intrinsic spiritual hierarchy;
וַחֲכָמִים הָפְכוּ הַסֵּדֶר כְּפִי סֵדֶר הָאֱנוֹשִׁי בְּהַגָּעָתוֹ אֶל הַמַּעֲלָה.
whereas the Sages inverted the order to follow the practical human path of gradual spiritual ascent.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת דִּבְרָכוֹת (י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "מְנָא יָדְעָה" — פֵּרוּשׁ, שֶׁ"אִישׁ קָדוֹשׁ", דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מֻגְדָּר מִתַּאֲווֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;

And this is the inner core of the dispute in Berakhot (10b) regarding the Shunammite woman: "From where did she know" that Elisha was a holy man—meaning fenced off from physical lusts as explained above;

חֵלֶק אֶחָד [אָמַר]: לֹא רָאֲתָה זְבוּב, רָצָה לוֹמַר תִּקּוּן תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דִּמְדַמֶּה זְבוּב בַּקְּעָרָה לְסוֹטָה, דִּזְבוּב מְאִיסוּתָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּגִטִּין (צ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳);
one opinion states: she never saw a fly upon his table, alluding to the mastery over the desire for food, a fly in the bowl being likened to a sotah, representing repulsive gluttony (Gittin 90b);

וְגַם עִנְיַן פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּשָׁם "זְבוּב" וְ"נִימָא" הוּא כַּמְכֻוָּן הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל: נִימָא רָצָה לוֹמַר כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה מִתַּאֲוַת עֲרָיוֹת, וְהוּא סַכָּנְתָא, "אֵשׁ בִּנְעֹרֶת וְאַתָּה מְהַבְהֲבָהּ";
and the dispute there between a "fly" and a "hair" aligns with this: a hair denotes a strand-thin trace of sexual passion, which is acute danger, like holding flame to flax;
וְאַסִּיק: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים, זְבוּב בַּתְּחִלָּה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "מִי גָּרַם לָעֲבֵירָה? יַיִן", שֶׁהוּא הַקּוֹדֵם, וְלֹא הִקְפִּיד רַק אַנִּימָא.
concluding that both are the words of the living God: the fly appears first—as they taught: "What caused the transgression? Wine"—and he objected only to the hair.
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ, שֶׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה גַּרְגְּרָנוּת וְהַרְגָּשַׁת תַּאֲוָה גּוּפָנִית, וּמִזֶּה הֵבִינָה גַּם כֵּן עַל תַּאֲוָה שְׁנִיָּה;
And this is not the place to elaborate: she observed no gluttony or coarse physical desire at his table, deducing from this his mastery over the second lust;
וְחֵלֶק אֶחָד לְהֵיפֶךְ, שֶׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה קֶרִי וְכוּלֵי, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן תַּאֲוָה שְׁנִיָּה, וּכְסֵדֶר חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה; וְלַלָּשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן הוּא כְּסֵדֶר הַתּוֹרָה.

while the other opinion argues the reverse: she never saw an unholy nocturnal emission on his sheets, and how much more so the second appetite, following the Sages' pedagogical order; the first formulation reflecting the Torah's intrinsic hierarchy.

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 1: “The Gemara asks how she knew, for holiness of the covenant concerns private matters that are not visible. One says that she never saw a fly on his table: she recognized in his eating the absence of the inclination’s craving, which is compared to a fly, and from this knew that he was also guarded in matters of intimacy. Another says that she spread a linen sheet for him and saw no seminal emission on it. This is something a person cannot ensure by his own effort; rather, he is guarded from above in proportion to how he sanctifies himself below. One who sanctifies himself below to the limit of human ability is sanctified above through divine power, which has no limit, and is rescued even from impurities inherent in the natural conditions of this world.”

paragraphs.text: Gittin 6b:11-15: “Concerning the concubine at Givah, Rabbi Evyatar said that her husband found a fly, while Rabbi Yonatan said he found a hair. Rabbi Evyatar met Eliyahu and asked what the Holy One was doing. He answered that He was discussing this passage: ‘Evyatar My son says this; Yonatan My son says this.’ Are there doubts before Heaven? Eliyahu answered: Both are the words of the living God. He found a fly and did not take offense; he found a hair and did take offense. Rav Yehuda explained: A fly in the dish and a hair in the intimate area—the fly was repulsive, while the hair presented danger. Others say both were in the dish: the fly was accidental, while the hair reflected carelessness. Rav Chisda said: A person must never impose excessive fear within his household.”

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 47: “The Kohen Gadol was the soul chosen from all Israel in wisdom and fear of sin. Many safeguards had preceded his service—in food, drink, and sleep—and Israel’s prayers assisted him. Why, then, was freedom from a seminal emission counted as a miracle? Because on this day he entered the place where the light of Hashem’s will shines without garment. His service had to be directed beyond what was known, and he could not enter with an independent conception of his own. All the preparations made beforehand were to leave an enduring effect afterward; in the moment of entering within, his own prayer was absent. The Shechinah spoke through his throat. A person’s essential capacity to receive is when he removes his own separate wishes and directs his whole desire to the simple divine will.”

p: וְתַקָּנָה כְּלָלִית לַתַּאֲווֹת הוּא עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק "וְעֵץ חַיִּים תַּאֲוָה בָאָה" [מִשְׁלֵי י״ג:י״ב];
And the universal remedy for lusts is intense engagement in Torah, as I have written elsewhere on the verse "and a tree of life is desire fulfilled" [Proverbs 13:12];
וּלְשׁוֹן הָרַמְבַּ״ם בְּהִלְכוֹת אִסּוּרֵי בִּיאָה [פֶּרֶק כ״ב הֲלָכָה כ״א], שֶׁאֵין הַתַּאֲווֹת מְצוּיוֹת אֶלָּא בְּלֵב פָּנוּי מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;
and in the words of Maimonides (Hilchot Issurei Biah 22:21): lusts are found only in a heart vacated of words of Torah;
וְזֶהוּ הָרֶמֶז בִּנְטִילַת יָדַיִם קֹדֶם אֲכִילָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל אוֹת א׳.
which is the esoteric meaning of washing hands prior to eating, as explained above in Section 1.
אָמְנָם הָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא, וּבְלֵב מָלֵא תַּאֲווֹת וַחֲמוּדוֹת הָעוֹלָם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה לִכָּנֵס,
Nevertheless, these two are mutually dependent: into a heart clogged with lusts and worldly attachments it is impossible for words of Torah to enter,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמ״ח דְּבָרִים שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִקְנֵית, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵירוּבִין [נ״ה עַמּוּד א׳]: אִם מֵשִׂים עַצְמוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְכוּלֵי וְאִם לָאו וְכוּלֵי.
as listed among the forty-eight qualifications for acquiring Torah, and in Eruvin [55a]: if one makes himself humble like a wilderness, the Torah is given to him, and if not, it departs.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם דָּבָר זֶה הוּא הָעֵצָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה לְתַקֵּן עַצְמוֹ בְּתַאֲוֹת לִבּוֹ, וְהוּא הָעִקָּר שֶׁהַכֹּל תָּלוּי בּוֹ;
In any event, Torah study is the primary counsel for rectifying the cravings of the heart, the central foundation upon which everything depends;

וּלְכָךְ עַם הָאָרֶץ אָסוּר לֶאֱכֹל בָּשָׂר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּפְסָחִים (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳), כִּי אָמְרוּ: אֵין שִׂמְחָה אֶלָּא בְּבָשָׂר, וְזֶהוּ תֹּקֶף הַתַּעֲנוּג, לְכָךְ אָסוּר, רַק לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם הַמֻּגְדָּר מִמֶּנּוּ.

which is why an unlettered boor (am ha'aretz) is forbidden to eat meat (Pesachim 49b), for they taught: "There is no joy except with meat," which is the apex of physical pleasure and therefore forbidden to him, permitted only to the scholar protected by self-restraint.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 184: “The beginning of words of Torah is desire, as it says, ‘His desire is in Hashem’s Torah.’ Then it is called Hashem’s Torah; afterward comes attainment, called ‘in his Torah he meditates.’ Desire is greater at the beginning. Attainment comes from Hashem, for Hashem gives wisdom, and everything is in Heaven’s hands except fear of Heaven. The awakening from below through desire and will is in the person’s hands. Nevertheless, Hashem makes ‘Hashem’s Torah’ into ‘his Torah’ and calls the innovations in Torah his own.”

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 109a: “The Sages taught: A person must gladden his children and household on the festival, as it says, ‘You shall rejoice on your festival.’ With what does he gladden them? With wine. Rabbi Yehuda says: Men with what suits them, and women with what suits them. Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: When the Temple stood, joy was only with meat, as it says, ‘You shall slaughter peace-offerings and eat there, and rejoice before Hashem your God.’ Now that the Temple does not stand, joy is only with wine, as it says, ‘Wine gladdens the heart of man.’”

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Bamidbar 4: “‘The greatness of study is that it brings to action.’ My honored grandfather and master explained that its main intention is deeper than the plain meaning. p: הָעֵצָה הַשְּׁנִיָּה: הַמְּתִינוּת; כִּי יְסוֹד תֹּקֶף הַתַּאֲוָה הַמְּהִירוּת, שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִבְלֹעַ וּלְהַשְׁלִים תַּאֲוָתוֹ חִישׁ,
The second counsel is patience and deliberation (metinut); for the bedrock of raging lust is haste, rushing to swallow and satisfy its craving instantly,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבֵיצָה [כ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳]: נְטִיעָה מְקַטַּעַת רַגְלֵיהֶן דְּקַצָּבַיָּא וּדְבוֹעֲלֵי נִדּוֹת, שֶׁהֵם שְׁתֵּי תַּאֲווֹת הָרָאשִׁיּוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרוֹת הַבָּאִים מִמְּהִירוּת.
as stated in Beitzah [25b]: a newly planted tree trips up the feet of butchers and those who cohabit with menstruant women—the two primal lusts mentioned above, fueled by reckless speed.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּחֻלִּין (פ״ד עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁתּוֹרָה לִמְּדָה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁלֹּא יֹאכַל אָדָם בָּשָׂר אֶלָּא בְּהַזְמָנָה;
And our Sages taught in Chullin (84a) that the Torah teaches proper conduct: a person should not eat meat except through preparation;
וּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים רֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳, ב׳) בְּכָל אֲכִילָה דְּשָׁם: "נִכְנַס" וְ"נִכְנָסִין", לוֹמַר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ כְּנִיסָה וַהֲכָנָה לַאֲכִילָה,
and the language of the Sages at the start of Berakhot (2a) regarding meals repeatedly uses "enters" and "they enter," indicating that eating requires deliberate entry and mindful preparation;
וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּאֲכִילַת עָנִי אָמַר שָׁם לְשׁוֹן "נִכְנַס" (וְעַיֵּן שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "מִשָּׁעָה", וְיְעֻיַּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּחִדּוּשַׁי לְשָׁם);
and even regarding the pauper's meal the Gemara uses the term "enters" (see Tosafot there, s.v. mishe'ah, and my novellae on that passage);
וְגַם בַּאֲכִילַת תְּרוּמָה וְשֶׁל שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהֵם אֲכִילַת מִצְוָה, נֶאֱמַר גַּם כֵּן "נִכְנָסִין", שֶׁצְּרִיכִין הֲכָנָה, וְלֹא אֲכִילַת עֲרַאי כַּאֲכִילַת זוֹלֵל וְסוֹבֵא שֶׁחוֹטֵף וְאוֹכֵל.

and likewise regarding terumah and Shabbat meals—which are mitzvah meals—the term "they enter" is used, requiring holy preparation rather than casual indulgence like a glutton who snatches and devours.
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵירוּבִין (נ״ד עַמּוּד א׳): "חֲטֹף וֶאֱכוֹל וְכוּלֵי", נִרְאֶה כִּי יֵשׁ חִלּוּקִים בִּבְנֵי אָדָם,
And what is stated in Eruvin (54a): "Snatch and eat, snatch and drink," appears to reflect distinctions between individuals:

שֶׁמִּי שֶׁכְּבָר אָדוּק וְדָבוּק בְּמַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אָז יִהְיֶה חוֹטֵף וְאוֹכֵל, דֻּגְמַת בֵּי הִלּוּלֵי שֶׁהַמְכֻוָּן עִנְיָן אַחֵר שֶׁעָסוּק בְּשִׂמְחָתוֹ, רַק בֵּין כָּךְ חוֹטֵף וְאוֹכֵל,

one whose thoughts are already firmly bound to words of Torah may snatch and eat, like a guest at a wedding feast whose primary focus is celebrating the groom and bride, merely snatching a morsel along the way,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין מָקוֹם מֵיחוּשׁ וַחֲשָׁד כְּלָל לְתַאֲוֹת לְבָבוֹ, וּבָטוּחַ בָּהֶם שֶׁדְּבוּקִים רַק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה.
since there is no suspicion of lust in his heart, confident that his faculties are cleaving exclusively to Torah and divine service.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 1: “A person’s initial entry into the service of Hashem must be in haste, as we find with the Pesach of Egypt, which was eaten in haste, unlike the Pesach of later generations. At the beginning, to detach himself from the desires of this world to which he is bound, he must guard the moment in which a desire for Hashem awakens, and hasten at that moment to escape them, perhaps successfully. Afterward he should proceed with deliberation and slowly, like the Pesach of later generations.”

p: הַשֻּׁלְחָן דּוֹמֶה לַמִּזְבֵּחַ כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשִׁלְהֵי חֲגִיגָה [כ״ז עַמּוּד א׳], וּבְהֵיפֶךְ אָמַר בְּאָבוֹת [פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה ג׳]: "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים", דְּהַיְינוּ תִּקְרֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, כִּמְפֹרָשׁ בִּתְהִלִּים [ק״ו:כ״ח] דְּנִקְרָא "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּחֻלִּין [י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳].

The table resembles the altar, as stated at the end of Chagigah [27a]; conversely, Pirkei Avot [3:3] states that a table lacking Torah discourse is full of "sacrifices of the dead"—meaning offerings to idolatry, as explicit in Psalms and cited in the first chapter of Chullin [13b].
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַהֲנָאָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם מִן הַמַּאֲכָל, אִם נִכְנֶסֶת לַנֶּפֶשׁ הָאֱלֹהִית וְחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל שֶׁבּוֹ,
This is because the pleasure a person derives from food, if channeled into the divine soul and the transcendent divine spark within him—

הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא אֶת הַמַּאֲכָל הַזֶּה וּמְחַיֵּהוּ וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ הֲוָיָה וְקִיּוּם, וְהוּא נוֹתֵן בּוֹ טַעַם וַהֲנָאָה, וְנוֹתֵן לָאָדָם חֵשֶׁק שֶׁיִּתְאַוֶּה לוֹ וְשֶׁיִּטְעַם בּוֹ טַעַם טוֹב וְשֶׁיּוֹסִיף בְּכֹחוֹ וְחִיּוּתוֹ;

meaning when he recognizes that the Blessed Name created this food, sustains it, grants it existence, infuses it with flavor and pleasure, and grants man the appetite to relish it and draw physical strength and vitality from it;
כְּשֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁזֶּה הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה, מֵאִיר בַּלֵּב בְּלִי הַטְעָיָה בְּנַפְשׁוֹ לַחְשֹׁב דִּמְיוֹן דֶּרֶךְ הַעֲבָרָה בְּעָלְמָא, לְהַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה
when he perceives with crystal clarity that everything originates from the Blessed Name, illuminating his heart without self-deception or superficial fantasy—

הִנֵּה הַכָּרָה זוֹ הוּא מִכֹּחַ הַחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ וְצַד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ, וְאוֹתוֹ הַצַּד נִתְגַּבֵּר, וַהֲנָאַת אוֹתוֹ הַצַּד הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֲנָאַת הַקָּרְבָּן שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, כִּי שָׁוֶה הוּא הַחֵלֶק עִם הַכֹּל.

this recognition derives from the divine soul and his good inclination, which triumphs, making that physical pleasure identical to the pleasing aroma of a holy sacrifice on high, for the individual spark is identical with the All.
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁשּׁוֹכֵחַ זֶה וְאוֹכֵל לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ לְמִלּוּי הַתַּאֲוָה, זֶהוּ מִצַּד נֶפֶשׁ הַמִּתְאַוָּה הַבְּהֵמִית שֶׁבָּאָדָם, וּכְאִלּוּ מַקְרִיב לָהּ קָרְבָּן;
But when he forgets this and eats for self-indulgence to gratify physical cravings, it stems from the animalistic soul within man, as though he were offering a sacrifice to it;
וְזֶהוּ "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים" מַמָּשׁ, שֶׁכֹּחַ זֶה וְתַאֲוָה זוֹ הוּא כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: רְשָׁעִים בְּחַיֵּיהֶם קְרוּיִים מֵתִים, שֶׁהַחִיּוּת הוּא דִּמְיוֹן בְּעָלְמָא אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא מִיתָה,

and this is literally "sacrifices of the dead," for this lust aligns with the dictum: "The wicked in their lifetimes are called dead," their apparent vitality being a hollow illusion while in truth it is death,
וְהַקְרָבָתָהּ הוּא "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים" וְתִקְרֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה: הַשִּׁכְחָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִלּוּי כֹּחַ אַחֵר חוּץ מִכֹּחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and feeding it constitutes idolatrous offerings, for the essence of idolatry is forgetting the Blessed Name and nurturing an alien power outside of Him.
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה הוּא שֻׁלְחָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ הוּא הַמְבָרֵר שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי חָכְמָה לְשׁוֹן הַכָּרָה כַּיָּדוּעַ;
And the remedy for this is a table crowned with words of Torah, whose inner light clarifies and acknowledges that all comes from Hashem, Chochmah denoting perception (hakarah);
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן כַּוָּנַת הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ חֲכָמִים קֹדֶם אֲכִילָה, שֶׁעִנְיָנָהּ הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַבּוֹרֵא וּמְהַוֶּה מַאֲכָל זֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַאֲכָל.

and this is likewise the purpose of the blessings instituted before eating: consciously recognizing that the Blessed Name is the Creator who continually sustains this substance so that it may serve as food.

paragraphs.text: Chullin 13b: “The slaughter of an idolater is a carcass. Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: The slaughter of a sectarian is for idolatry; his bread is like the bread of a Samaritan, his wine is libation wine, and his books are the books of diviners. The Gemara distinguishes this from ordinary gentile slaughter and does not presume every ordinary gentile act to be an idolatrous offering.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Achrei Mot 7:4: “The Holy One foresaw the destruction of the Temple: Through what will you obtain atonement? Occupy yourselves with words of Torah, which are compared to offerings, as the prophet says, ‘Take words with you.’ Since Torah is compared to offerings, a sanctuary is needed in which to offer them. When they take words of Torah, they themselves become a Mishkan and a Temple. The Midrash compares Torah to the wine, bread, and oil offered on the altar: ‘Drink the wine I have mixed,’ ‘Come, eat of My bread,’ and ‘Let oil not be lacking upon your head.’ These words are the Oral Torah, the word of Hashem expressed in halakhah. On Shabbat one can merit that the heart become a Mishkan for the Shechinah.”

p: לְהַעֲלוֹת כָּל מַאֲכָלִים מִצּוֹמֵחַ הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הָאֱמוּנָה לְבַד בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְעַל יְדֵי הַבְּרָכָה מִקֹּדֶם שֶׁמַּאֲמִין שֶׁ"לַה' הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ";

Elevating vegetarian foods derived from the botanical kingdom (tzome'ach) requires simple faith alone in the Blessed Name, and reciting the prior blessing affirming that "the earth is Hashem's and the fullness thereof";
וּלְכָךְ "אֱמוּנַת" — זֶה סֵדֶר זְרָעִים, וְנִקְבְּעָה מַסֶּכֶת בְּרָכוֹת בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ;
which is why "Faith" corresponds to the Order of Zera'im (Seeds), opening with Tractate Berakhot;

וְזֶהוּ הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁל הַעֲלָאַת כָּל מִינֵי הַזְּרָעִים לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי קִיּוּם הַמִּצְוֹת הַכְּתוּבוֹת בָּהֶם וְהַבְּרָכָה מִקֹּדֶם, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁהַכֹּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, בֶּאֱמוּנָה הַפְּשׁוּטָה הַקְּבוּעָה בְּלֵב כָּל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשַׁבָּת [צ״ז עַמּוּד א׳] שֶׁהֵם "מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים", וּלְכָךְ הוּתַר אֲפִילּוּ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ.

this being the order of elevating plant life to Hashem through the agricultural commandments and the prior blessing, founded upon the simple faith innate to every Jew (Shabbat 97a: "believers, children of believers"), which is why produce is permitted even to an unlettered commoner.
אֲבָל אֲכִילַת בָּשָׂר אָסוּר, רַק לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם;
But eating meat is forbidden, permitted only to a Torah scholar;

וְלָכֵן נִקְבְּעָה מַסֶּכֶת חֻלִּין בְּסֵדֶר קָדָשִׁים, דְּלֹא הוּתַר אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁאוֹכֵל חֻלִּין עַל טָהֳרַת קֹדֶשׁ, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁשֻּׁלְחָנוֹ דּוֹמֶה לַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְהַבָּשָׂר שֶׁאוֹכֵל כְּקָרְבָּן וּבְשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ.

which is why Tractate Chullin was codified within the Order of Kodashim (Holy Things), being sanctioned only for one who partakes of mundane food in the purity of consecrated meat, whose table resembles the altar and whose meat is like a holy sacrifice.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה;
And this elevation is possible solely through words of Torah, as stated: since the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One has nothing in His world except the four cubits of Halakhah;

וּכְשֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה שֻׁלְחָנוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה, אָז הוּא נַעֲשָׂה דֻּגְמַת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וּמִזְבֵּחַ, וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא אוֹכֵל הוּא דֻּגְמַת כֹּהֲנִים, "כִּי קָא זָכוּ — מִשֻּׁלְחַן גָּבוֹהַּ קָא זָכוּ";
and when his table becomes four cubits of Halakhah, it embodies the Temple and the altar, his eating mirroring the priests who acquire their portions directly from the Table of the Most High;

שֶׁהַחֵלֶב וְהַדָּם, רָצָה לוֹמַר עִקַּר הַחִיּוּת שֶׁבַּמַּאֲכָל וְהַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּאָדָם לוֹ, הוּעֲלָה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה (שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לְאֵשׁ שֶׁהוּא אֵשׁ הַמַּעֲרָכָה),
so that the fat and the blood—meaning the vital essence of the food and the human craving for it—are elevated to Hashem through the fire of Torah (the fire of the altar pile),
שֶׁמַּכִּיר עַל יָדוֹ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן הַחִיּוּת בַּמַּאֲכָל, וְהַנּוֹתֵן הַתַּאֲוָה לָאָדָם וְהַחֵשֶׁק לְזֶה הַמַּאֲכָל לְקַיֵּם נַפְשׁוֹ.
recognizing that the Blessed Name infuses life into the nourishment and instills within man the hunger to sustain his soul.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 2: “‘Blessings are upon the head of the righteous.’ Therefore Berakhot begins the six Orders, for the foundation of everything is ‘Know the God of your father,’ and afterward ‘serve Him’: one must know whom he serves. This is the blessing before every deed, to unite all his actions with Hashem: ‘Know Him in all your ways.’ A blessing is founded upon knowing whom one blesses. This is the beginning of entry into Torah: ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem.’ All blessings begin with direct address, so that at the beginning Hashem should be before the person’s eyes as though standing over him and commanding him; their conclusion is in the third person, for He immediately becomes concealed, touching and not touching.”

p: עַל יְדֵי מַאֲכָל אֶחָד וּסְעוּדָה אַחַת בַּשָּׁבוּעַ (אוֹ סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת) שֶׁאוֹכֵל בְּכַוָּנָה הָרְאוּיָה לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם, וּלְהַעֲלוֹת כֹּחוֹת נֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מִתְעַלִּים כָּל הַמַּאֲכָלִים וְהַסְּעוּדוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ;

Through a single meal during the week (or a Shabbat meal) eaten with pristine devotion for the sake of Heaven to elevate animalistic soul-powers to the Blessed Name, all of one's other meals become elevated;
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חַכְמֵי הָאֱמֶת בִּתְפִלָּה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה אַחַת מַעֲלֶה כָּל הַתְּפִלּוֹת הַפְּסוּלוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הַשָּׁנָה;
just as the masters of Kabbalah taught concerning prayer: that through one fervent prayer one elevates all flawed prayers of the entire year;

וּתְפִלָּה הוּא דֻּגְמַת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת, וְכֵן הָאֲכִילָה (וּגְדוֹלָה מַעֲלַת הָאֲכִילָה כְּשֶׁהִיא עַל טָהֳרַת קֹדֶשׁ מִן הַתְּפִלָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מִמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה גַּבֵּי יִצְחָק: אִם לְקָרְבָּנְךָ הִזְמִין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, לְמַאֲכָלְךָ לֹא כָּל שֶׁכֵּן?),

and prayer mirrors the sacrifices, as does eating (consecrated eating being greater even than prayer, as our Sages noted regarding Isaac: "If for your sacrifice the Holy One provided, how much more so for your food!"),
שֶׁהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "וַיִּקַץ כְּיָשֵׁן", הַפִּגּוּל — וּמָצָא מִין אֶת מִינוֹ וְנֵעוֹר.
operating like the dictum: "And he awoke as one out of sleep," where flawed matter reunites with its elevated counterpart and is revived.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ, כָּל הָאֲכִילוֹת שֶׁל אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הוּא דֻּגְמַת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת, רַק כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְבֹרָר לָאָדָם בְּכַוָּנַת לִבּוֹ וּמֹחוֹ הוּא דֻּגְמַת יָשֵׁן,
For in absolute truth, all eating of an Israelite mirrors holy sacrifices, only that when unclarified by conscious intent of heart and mind, it resembles slumber;

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "בְּשׁוּב ה' וְגוֹמֵר הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים", וְאִיכָּא אִינָשׁ דְּנָיֵים שִׁבְעִים שְׁנִין, שֶׁהֵם יְמֵי שְׁנוֹתֵינוּ בָּהֶם, כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְעוֹרֵר מִתַּרְדֵּמַת הַזְּמָן, הֲרֵי הוּא כְּיָשֵׁן;
as written: "When Hashem returns the captivity of Zion, we were like dreamers," a person slumbering through his seventy years if he fails to awaken from temporal sleep;

כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה אִסּוּרִים מַמָּשׁ רַק בְּהֶתֵּר, עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה [ס״ה עַמּוּד א׳]: יָכוֹל יְגָרֶה עַצְמוֹ בְּשֵׁנָה (וְכַיָּדוּעַ דְּהַהֶתֵּר הוּא מִקְּלִפַּת נֹגַהּ שֶׁהוּא סוֹד הַתַּרְגּוּם, בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא תַּרְדֵּמָה),
when committing no outright sin but indulging in permitted matter—permissible realms deriving from Kelipat Nogah (targum equaling tardemah, 649)—
וְאָמַר: יוֹשֵׁב בָּטֵל כְּיָשֵׁן דָּמֵי.
where one who sits idle is considered asleep.

וּכְשֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְהִתְעוֹרֵר פַּעַם אַחַת מִשְּׁנָתוֹ, יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַתַּרְדֵּמוֹת, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תַּרְדֵּמָה שֶׁל נְבוּאָה, כִּדְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה דְּג׳ תַּרְדֵּמוֹת הֵן וְיֵשׁ שֶׁל נְבוּאָה;
And when he merits to awaken once from his slumber, he can rectify all prior sleep into the sleep of prophecy (Bereishit Rabbah: three types of deep slumber, including prophecy);
כִּי אָז נְבוּאָה בָּאָה עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיִצְחָק
for prophecy was drawn down through food and drink, as with Isaac

(וְכֵן כָּל תַּאֲווֹת דְּהֶתֵּר כְּעִנְיַן "כְּנַגֵּן הַמְנַגֵּן", וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: רַבָּה פָּתַח בְּמִילֵי דִּבְדִיחוּתָא, רַק שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא אַחַר כָּךְ שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה, כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה אַחַר כָּךְ מִצְוָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהַבְּדִיחוּתָא, וְכָל הַהֲנָאוֹת שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִתְעַלֵּית גַּם הֲנָאָה זוֹ לִהְיוֹת שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה);
(just as Elisha called for a musician, or Rabbah opened his lecture with humorous words to open the heart, worldly pleasures being elevated into the joy of a mitzvah);

וְכֵן כָּל שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר פַּעַם אַחַת יוּכַל לְהַעֲלוֹת כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל הֶתֵּר וְדִבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁעָשָׂה (וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת בְּלֹא כַּוָּנָה וְחִיּוּת) מִקֹּדֶם, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ פַּעַם אַחֶרֶת עִם חִיּוּת וְכַוָּנָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
and so, one who awakens once can elevate all previous permissible acts (and certainly mitzvot done without fervor) by performing them afresh with vitality and intent for Heaven.
וּבְיוֹתֵר בַּאֲכִילָה שֶׁהִיא דֻּגְמַת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת (שֶׁבָּהֶם נוֹהֵג דִּין הַגְּרִירָה כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשַׁבָּת), וַאֲכִילָה גּוֹרֶרֶת אֲכִילָה לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹתָהּ.
Especially in eating, which mirrors sacrifices (governed by the laws of dragging/association in Shabbat): one sanctified meal drags all others to become like it.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 71a:1-3: “Harvesting draws harvesting after it, and grinding draws grinding after it. Abaye said: Grinding also draws grinding after it, for it is one designation of grinding. The Gemara discusses one who ate two olive-bulks of forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness, learned of one, and ate a third during the remaining lapse. If he brought an offering for the middle one, all were atoned for. Abaye said: Even if he brought an offering for any one of them, all were atoned for. The discussion distinguishes ‘drawing after’ from ‘drawing after what was itself drawn after.’”

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 32: “Abaye recounts the earlier stages in which he took priestly gifts eagerly, then asked for them, and finally refrained. My father explained that through his final clarification it became clear retroactively that his initial eagerness, too, had been love of the mitzvah. So it is with the ninth and tenth: through the great clarification of the tenth, when a person restricts himself, it becomes clear that his previous bodily needs also contained the honor of Heaven. One might have expected fasting first and eating afterward. Here Hashem wills that eating and drinking come first, so that the person should draw the entire expansion of his needs into holiness. ‘With this Aharon shall enter the holy place’—with that very expansion of the whole year he shall enter.”

p: ג׳ שֵׁמוֹת לַמַּאֲכָל: "מַאֲכָל", וְהוּא מִצַּד עַצְמוּת הַמַּאֲכָל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה שֶׁרָאוּי לַאֲכִילַת אָדָם וּלְהַחֲיוֹת נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם, מִצַּד נִיצוֹץ חִיּוּת הַשַּׁיָּךְ לְנֶפֶשׁ אָדָם שֶׁקָּבַע בּוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְקַיֵּם חִיּוּת הָאָדָם בְּקִרְבּוֹ;
There are three names for food: Ma'achal (Food)—from the perspective of the food's essence, endowed with the capacity to sustain human life through a divine spark of vitality embedded by Hashem;
וּ"מָזוֹן", הוּא מִצַּד הָאָדָם הַנִּיזּוֹן וּמְקַבֵּל הַחִיּוּת מִמֶּנּוּ;
and Mazon (Sustenance)—from the perspective of the human recipient being nourished by it;
וְ"טֶרֶף", הוּא לְשׁוֹן חֲטִיפָה, וְהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַעֲלָאַת אוֹתוֹ נִיצוֹץ חִיּוּת לִמְקוֹרוֹ כְּשֶׁאוֹכְלוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁאָז הוּא דֻּגְמַת הַקָּרְבָּן.
and Teref (Prey/Snatching)—connoting seizing, referring to elevating that spark of vitality to its supernal source when eaten in holiness like a sacrifice.
וְהַמִּזְבֵּחַ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה [יוֹמָא י״ב עַמּוּד א׳] בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל טוֹרֵף — "בִּנְיָמִין זְאֵב יִטְרָף", וְנִקְרָא בְּשִׁלְהֵי סֻכָּה [נ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳] "לוּקוֹס לוּקוֹס" [זְאֵב];
And the altar stood in the territory of Benjamin the predator—"Benjamin is a wolf that ravenously seizes"—addressed at the end of Sukkah [56b] as "Lukos, Lukos" (Wolf, Wolf);

וְהַיְינוּ כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת מִתְעַלֵּית הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַבְּהֵמִית, וְהִיא הָעֲשׁוּקָה גּוֹ טִיקְלָא שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים "עֲשׁוּקִים" בְּסָבָא דְּמִשְׁפָּטִים [זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ צ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳], כִּי הוּא בָּא בִּגְזֵלָה וּבַחֲטִיפָה;
because through sacrifices the animal soul is elevated, rescuing the sparks trapped within unholy shells (the "oppressed" in Sava d'Mishpatim, Zohar II:95b) through spiritual snatching;
וְכֵן צָרִיךְ לְהִתְקוֹמֵם נֶגְדּוֹ בַּחֲטִיפָה, כְּטַעַם: יַרְגִּיז אָדָם יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע, בְּהַרְגָּזָה וְכֹחַ, כְּטַעַם "אֵיזֶהוּ גִּבּוֹר וְכוּלֵי";

so must man aggressively conquer it, as in "A man should always incite the good inclination against the evil inclination" (Berakhot 5a), through mighty exertion ("Who is mighty? He who conquers his impulse");
וְכֵן בַּזֹּהַר נִקְרָא בְּכָל מָקוֹם מִלְחָמָה בַּחֲרָבוֹת וּקְשָׁתוֹת, וְנִקְרָא שְׁעַת אֲכִילָה "שְׁעַת קְרָבָא";
called throughout the Zohar a battle waged with swords and bows, the hour of eating being "the hour of battle";

כִּי עֲלִיַּת הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת הוּא עַל יְדֵי נִצּוּחַ יֵצֶר טוֹב לְיֵצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁהַמַּאֲכָל שֶׁהוּא הַמְחַיֶּה הַגּוּף מְחַיֶּה רַק כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב וְהַיֵּצֶר טוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ וְלֹא כֹּחַ הָרָע, וְכֹחַ הַטּוֹב נוֹצֵחַ בַּמִּלְחָמָה לַחְטֹף הַנִּיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ וְחִיּוּת הַמַּאֲכָל לְחֶלְקוֹ.
for elevating sparks requires conquering the evil inclination, ensuring that the nourishment strengthens exclusively the good inclination and snatches the holy spark away from the unholy realm.
וְזֶה טַעַם "הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חֻקִּי" שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁכָּל עִסְקוֹ הָיָה בְּהַעֲלָאַת נִיצוֹצוֹת,
This is the mystery of "Feed me with my allotted bread (hatrifeni lechem chuki)" petitioned by King Solomon, whose lifework was elevating sparks,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בְּעִנְיַן הַנָּשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת שֶׁנָּשָׂא, וַהֲלִיכָתוֹ לְתַרְמוֹד לִמְקוֹם עֻזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר, הָיָה לַחְטֹף הַטּוֹב מִן הָרָע;
as written elsewhere regarding his marrying foreign wives and venturing to Tadmor (the dwelling of Uzza and Azael, Zohar) to snatch good from evil;

וּבִקֵּשׁ עַל הַמַּאֲכָל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן "טֶרֶף", וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי "לֶחֶם חֻקִּי", בְּהַגְדָּרָה, לֹא בְּרַעַבְתָנוּת וְשֶׁפַע תַּאֲוָה הַנִּקְרָא "עֹשֶׁר", וְלֹא בְּהַכְפָּנָה יְתֵרָה וְרֵישׁוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: הַיּוֹשֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא

asking that his food be teref (captured prey) through lechem chuki (allotted bread)—eaten in disciplined measure, neither in gluttonous indulgence ("wealth") nor in excessive fasting and self-deprivation ("poverty"), where one who fasts excessively is called a sinner—
פֵּרוּשׁ, שֶׁמְּחַסֵּר הַעֲלָאַת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה שֶׁבַּמַּאֲכָל לִמְקוֹמָהּ עַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילָה;
meaning that he deprives the holy sparks within food from being elevated through sanctified consumption;
וְרַק "בֶּטֶן רְשָׁעִים תֶּחְסָר", רָאוּי לֶאֱסֹר וּלְהִתְעַנּוֹת כְּדֵי לְכַלּוֹת הָרַעַבְתָנוּת;
and only where "the belly of the wicked shall suffer want" is fasting proper, in order to crush gluttony;
אֲבָל צַדִּיק שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַעַבְתָן וְשָׁטוּף בְּתַאֲוָה, "אוֹכֵל לְשֹׂבַע נַפְשׁוֹ", הַיְינוּ לֶחֶם חֻקִּי,
but a righteous person who is not submerged in lust "eats to the satisfaction of his soul"—namely, his allotted bread—
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ לְדַרְגַּת "הַטְרִיפֵנִי", שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹרֵף וְחוֹטֵף הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּרָע לְכַלֵּל בַּטּוֹב.
achieving the level of hatrifeni, seizing and snatching the good from within the bad to unite it with holiness.
וְזֶה טַעַם "טֶרֶף נָתַן לִירֵאָיו": הַיְּרֵאִים הֵם הַמֻּגְדָּרִים בְּתַאֲווֹת בְּיוֹתֵר, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לִכְלַל מְנִיעַת אֲכִילַת לֶחֶם חֻקִּי גַּם כֵּן,
And this is "He gives prey (teref) to those who fear Him": those who fear Him fence themselves stringently against lust, occasionally withholding even their allotted bread,
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן לָהֶם בְּמַתָּנָה "טֶרֶף", לֶאֱכֹל לֶחֶם חֻקִּי עַל כָּל פָּנִים, כְּדֵי לִטְרֹף אוֹתָם הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים שֶׁבַּמַּאֲכָל.
so the Holy One grants them teref as a divine gift, empowering them to eat their allotted bread in order to liberate those trapped holy sparks.
וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵירוּבִין [נ״ד עַמּוּד א׳]: "חֲטֹף וֶאֱכוֹל וְכוּלֵי, כְּהִלּוּלָא דָּמְיָא":
And this is the inner meaning of Eruvin [54a]: "Snatch and eat, snatch and drink, for this world is like a wedding feast":

פֵּרוּשׁ, הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא יִחוּד חָתָן וְכַלָּה, הַיְינוּ קַבָּלַת הָאָדָם הַשֶּׁפַע מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, זֶהוּ רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא עֵסֶק הָאָדָם בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְהַחֵשֶׁק,
meaning this world represents the union of Groom and Bride, where man draws divine influx through arousal from below (itaruta diletata) and sacred yearning,
וּמְקַבֵּל הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא וְהַמִּלּוּי דְּמַיִּין דּוּכְרִין לְעֻמָּתוֹ, וְהוּא הַחֲתֻנָּה;
receiving in turn the arousal from above (itaruta dile'eila) and supernal waters, which is the wedding;
וְ"אַגְרָא דְּבֵי הִלּוּלָא — מִילֵּי", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק: "אָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד" — לַעֲמַל פֶּה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה,
and "the reward of a wedding feast is words" (Berakhot 6b), matching Sanhedrin [99b]: "Man is born to toil—to the toil of the mouth in Torah and prayer,"
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם מְשַׂמְּחִים חָתָן וְכַלָּה, וּמְעוֹרְרִים מַיִּין נוּקְבִין בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בִּתְפִלָּה וּמַיִּין דּוּכְרִין דִּלְעֵילָא בַּתּוֹרָה;
gladdening Groom and Bride, arousing feminine waters (mayin nukvin) through prayer and supernal masculine waters (mayin duchrin) through Torah;

וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְיַחֵד יִחוּדִים גַּם כֵּן בַּאֲכִילָתוֹ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג הַנֹּכַח דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הַמְחַיֶּה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא "חֲטֹף וֶאֱכוֹל", שֶׁחוֹטֵף וְטוֹרֵף אוֹתָם הָעֲשׁוּקִים לְתוֹךְ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
and through this he effects unifications during meals, perceiving Hashem as the ultimate sustainer, thereby "snatching and eating"—rescuing trapped holy sparks into sanctity.
וּלְכָךְ מַסֶּכֶת נָזִיר שֶׁעִנְיָנָהּ הַגְדָּרַת הַתַּאֲווֹת מְסַיֶּמֶת: "חֲטֹף וּבָרֵיךְ",
Therefore Tractate Nazir, dedicated to mastering bodily desires, concludes with the phrase: "Snatch and bless,"
כִּי לִירֵאָיו הַמֻּגְדָּרִים בְּתַאֲווֹת נִתַּן הַחֲטִיפָה, וְעַל כֵּן "וּבָרֵיךְ", דְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן הַהוֹדָאָה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּשֶׁהוּא שָׂבֵעַ — זֶהוּ גְּמַר הַחֲטִיפָה.

for to the pious who conquer their lusts is granted the power to snatch sparks, culminating in "and bless"—Birkat HaMazon being the thanksgiving to Hashem upon satisfaction that seals this holy capture.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 12a:4-5: “What was in Yehuda’s portion? The Temple Mount, chambers, and courtyards. What was in Binyamin’s portion? The entrance hall, Sanctuary, and Holy of Holies. A strip extended from Yehuda’s portion into Binyamin’s portion, and the altar was built on it. p: מִצְוַת אֲכִילַת מַצָּה נוֹתֶנֶת קְדוּשָׁה בָּאֲכִילוֹת,
The commandment of eating matzah infuses holiness into all acts of eating,
כִּי כָּל מִצְוָה, בִּפְרָט אוֹתָהּ שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עָלֶיהָ "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ", מוֹסֶפֶת קְדוּשָׁה בָּאָדָם, וּבְיִחוּד בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר וְכֹחַ שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נַעֲשֵׂית,

for every commandment, especially one over which we recite the blessing "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us," increases holiness within a person, and particularly within that limb and faculty through which it is performed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה [פָּרָשָׁה כ״א:ה׳]: "עָשִׂיתָ חֲבִילוֹת עֲבֵרוֹת — עֲשֵׂה נֶגְדָּן חֲבִילוֹת מִצְוֹת... יָדַיִם וְכוּלֵי";
as our Sages of blessed memory said in Vayikra Rabbah [21:5]: "If you have made bundles of transgressions, make bundles of mitzvot to counter them... hands, etc.";

וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (בֹּא [מ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳]): יֵצֶר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר רָע — חָמֵץ וּמַצָּה, וְכֵן בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק הָרוֹאֶה [בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳]: "שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִסָּה",

and this is the underlying reason for what is written in the Zohar (Bo 40b): the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination correspond to matzah and chametz, and likewise in the phrasing of our Sages in the chapter HaRo'eh [Berakhot 17a]: "the yeast in the dough,"
דְּעִקַּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בַּאֲכִילָה כַּיָּדוּעַ מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: עֵץ הַדַּעַת חִטָּה הָיָה [בְּרָכוֹת מ׳ עַמּוּד א׳];
for the core of the evil inclination lies in eating, as is known from the primeval serpent, and our Sages said: the Tree of Knowledge was wheat [Berakhot 40a];
וְנֶגְדּוֹ אֲכִילַת מַצָּה נוֹתֶנֶת קְדוּשָׁה בְּכָל מַאֲכְלֵי לֶחֶם שֶׁל כָּל הַשָּׁנָה,
and opposing it, the eating of matzah imparts holiness to all bread-based foods of the entire year,
וַאֲכִילַת מָרוֹר בְּכָל מַאֲכְלֵי יְרָקוֹת,
and the eating of maror imparts holiness to all vegetable foods,
וַאֲכִילַת קָדָשִׁים בַּבָּשָׂר;
and the eating of consecrated sacrificial meat imparts holiness to all meat;
וְעַל כֵּן בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה עַם הָאָרֶץ אָסוּר לֶאֱכֹל בָּשָׂר, כִּי אֵין לָנוּ אֲכִילַת בָּשָׂר שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עָלָיו "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ",

and therefore in our present era an unlettered boor (am ha'aretz) is forbidden to eat meat, because we lack sacrificial meat over which we recite the blessing "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,"
רַק תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דְּאֵין צְרִיכִים לְקַדֵּשׁ גּוּפָם, שֶׁהֵן עַצְמָם קֹדֶשׁ,
except for Torah scholars, who do not need external actions to sanctify their bodies, for they themselves are holy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה [כְּתוּבוֹת ק״ה עַמּוּד ב׳]: "הַמְמַלֵּא גְּרוֹנָם וְכוּלֵי כִּמְנַסֵּךְ וְכוּלֵי", וְ"הַמֵּבִיא דּוֹרוֹן וְכוּלֵי כִּמְבִיא בִּכּוּרִים",
as our Sages of blessed memory said [Ketubot 105b]: "Whoever fills their throat [with wine] is as if he pours libations," and "Whoever brings a gift [to a scholar] is as if he offers first-fruits,"

וְכֵן אֲכִילָתָן כְּקָרְבָּן, כִּי הֵן עַצְמָם כַּמִּזְבֵּחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשִׁלְהֵי חֲגִיגָה [כ״ז עַמּוּד א׳] שֶׁכָּל גּוּפָם אֵשׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ" [יִרְמְיָהוּ כ״ג:כ״ט],

and so their eating is considered like a sacrifice, for they themselves are like the altar, as our Sages said at the conclusion of Chagigah [27a] that their entire body is fire, as it is said: "Is not My word like as a fire?" [Jeremiah 23:29],
פֵּרוּשׁ, שֶׁבַּדָּבָר שֶׁאָדָם מְחַשֵּׁב כֵּן הוּא כָּל גּוּפוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר רְאָיָה מִמַּקְלוֹת דְּיַעֲקֹב.
meaning that whatever a person meditates upon, such becomes his entire body, as I have written elsewhere citing proof from the peeled rods of Jacob.
וּבַזֹּהַר נִקְרָא מַצָּה "מֵיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָתָא" [חֵלֶק ב׳ מ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳], שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדָהּ לְרַפְּאוֹת אֶת הַקּוֹדֵם,
And in the Zohar [II, 40b] matzah is called "the food of healing," having the power to heal all that preceded it,
וְכֵן בְּכָל מִצְוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מִמִּדְרַשׁ רַבָּה "עָשִׂיתָ וְכוּלֵי", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה: "רִפְאוּת תְּהִי [לְשָׁרֶּךָ]" וְגוֹמֵר [מִשְׁלֵי ג׳:ח׳],
and so it is with all commandments as mentioned above from Midrash Rabbah ("If you have made bundles..."), and as it is written of words of Torah: "It shall be health to your navel" [Proverbs 3:8],

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וְהַאֲזַנְתָּ לְמִצְוֺתָיו וְגוֹמֵר [כִּי אֲנִי] ה' רֹפְאֶךָ" [שְׁמוֹת ט״ו:כ״ו], וְקֻשְׁיַת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "אִם אֵין מַכָּה [רְפוּאָה לָמָּה]" וְכוּלֵי, יְדוּעָה;

and as written: "and give ear to His commandments... for I am Hashem that heals you" [Exodus 15:26], where the difficulty raised by our Sages ("If there is no wound, why is healing needed?") is well known;
רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר רְפוּאָה דִּסְלִיחָה, וְכִדְאִיתָא בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ב׳ דִּמְגִלָּה [י״ז עַמּוּד ב׳] עַל "וְשָׁב וְרָפָא [לוֹ]" [יְשַׁעְיָהוּ ו׳:י׳].
rather, it denotes the healing of divine forgiveness, as stated at the beginning of the second chapter of Megillah [17b] regarding the verse "and return, and be healed" [Isaiah 6:10].
וְהַמַּחֲלָה הוּא מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר: עֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת נֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת, קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה;
And sickness operates measure for measure, as I have written elsewhere: the Ten Plagues correspond to the Ten Commandments, constituting a complete spiritual stature;
וּבִסְלִיחַת הָעֲוֹנוֹת מִמֵּילָא לֹא יָשׂוּם גּוּף הַמַּחֲלָה.
and upon the forgiveness of sins, the illness itself naturally does not take hold.
וּמַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת נֶגֶד דִּבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַכֹּל, וּמִצְרַיִם שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרַע,
And the Plague of the Firstborn corresponds to the commandment "I am [Hashem your God]," which is the root of all, while Egypt was the root of evil;
וּלְכָךְ בְּעֵת מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת אָכְלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל פֶּסַח, מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר, לְתַקֵּן כָּל מִינֵי אֲכִילוֹת, וְנִתְקַן הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ לְטוֹב;
and therefore at the time of the Plague of the Firstborn, Israel ate the Pesach offering, matzah, and maror to rectify all categories of eating, and the root was rectified for good;

וְנֶאֱמַר: "כָּל בֶּן נֵכָר לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ" [שְׁמוֹת י״ב:מ״ג], וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "אֲבָל אוֹכֵל בְּמַצָּה וּמָרוֹר", הוּא כְּדֵי לְהַמְצִיא תִּקּוּנִים אַף לַכּוֹפְרִים, דְּ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל [הוּא]".

and it is said: "no stranger shall eat thereof" [Exodus 12:43], which our Sages expounded: "yet he eats of matzah and maror," which is designed to provide rectifications even for deniers, since "even though he has sinned, he remains an Israelite."

וְהִנֵּה גְּאֻלַּת מִצְרַיִם הוּא עַל יְדֵי לְאַכְפַּיָּא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל "וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ" [שְׁמוֹת י״ג:י״ט], לָכֵן נִצְטַוּוּ עַל בִּעוּר חָמֵץ, וְהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן חֵרוּת מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע רַק בְּדֶרֶךְ הַסִּלּוּק לְגַמְרֵי, מִדַּת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר;

And behold, the redemption from Egypt was through suppression (le-akfaya), as I wrote elsewhere on "And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him" [Exodus 13:19], wherefore they were commanded concerning the destruction of chametz, attaining freedom from the evil inclination through complete banishment, the path of the completely righteous (tzaddik gamur);

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא זְבִיחַת הַיֵּצֶר בְּעִנְיַן לְאִתְהַפְּכָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּיִהְיֶה גַּם אָז יֵצֶר הָרָע לְחֶדְוָתָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, רַק דְּנִקְרָא לָבָן דְּאִתְלַבַּן וְכוּלֵי,

whereas in the ultimate future, the vanquishing of the inclination will be through transformation (le-ithapcha), as stated in Midrash HaNe'elam that the evil impulse will then persist for the joyful celebration of Torah, renamed "Laban" because it is whitened into purity,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר דְּזֶה סוֹד סְעוּדַת לִוְיָתָן וְשׁוֹר הַבָּר, שֶׁהֵם יִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת וּדְעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מֵהֶם מַאֲכָל טוֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "טוֹב מְאֹד" — זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע [בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ט׳:ז׳], עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה זֶה בְּמִצְרַיִם.

and as I wrote elsewhere, this is the mystery of the banquet of Leviathan and the Wild Ox, which represent the inclinations for sexual immorality and idolatry, transformed into exquisite food, fulfilling "very good—this is the evil inclination" [Bereishit Rabbah 9:7], through King David, peace be upon him, who established the yoke of repentance, which had not yet occurred in Egypt.

וְאָמַר: "אֵיזֶהוּ עָשִׁיר? הַשָּׂמֵחַ [בְּחֶלְקוֹ]" [אָבוֹת ד׳:א׳], דְּעִקַּר עֲשִׁירוּת שִׂמְחָה, וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא מַצָּה "לֶחֶם עֹנִי", דְּלֵיכָּא חֶדְוָתָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בִּכְפִיַּת הַיֵּצֶר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וַיֵּלְכוּ וְגוֹמֵר וְלֹא מָצְאוּ מָיִם" [שְׁמוֹת ט״ו:כ״ב], וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: זוֹ תּוֹרָה [בָּבָא קַמָּא י״ז עַמּוּד א׳];

And the Sages said: "Who is wealthy? He who rejoices [in his portion]" [Avot 4:1], for the core of wealth is joy; therefore matzah is termed "the bread of poverty" (lechem oni), because boundless joy of Torah is absent during the mere suppression of the inclination, as written: "and they went... and found no water," expounded as Torah [Bava Kamma 17a];
וְלָכֵן מַרְבִּים בְּחֻמְרוֹת וְדִקְדּוּקִים בְּעִנְיְנֵי הַפֶּסַח יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַמִּצְוֹת, כְּמִדָּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים מְדַקְדְּקִים כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה.
and therefore we multiply stringencies and meticulous fences regarding Pesach more than all other commandments, mirroring the standard of the righteous who are scrutinized like a hair's breadth.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּעִנְיַן מְכִירַת הֶחָמֵץ שֶׁהוּא בִּעוּרוֹ מְקִילִין הַרְבֵּה, וְכָל עִקָּרוֹ הַעֲרָמָה כַּנּוֹדָע;
Yet nevertheless, regarding the sale of chametz, which constitutes its removal, we are extremely lenient, its legal framework functioning primarily as legal circumvention (ha'aramah), as is known;
הַיְינוּ דְּהַגַּם דְּיוֹסֵף הָיָה הַמְבַשֵּׂר לִגְאֻלַּת מִצְרַיִם: "פָּקֹד יִפְקֹד וְגוֹמֵר" [בְּרֵאשִׁית נ׳:כ״ד], בִּהְיוֹת הַגְּאֻלָּה בְּמִדָּתוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
meaning that although Joseph was the harbinger of Egypt's redemption ("God will surely visit you"), the redemption aligning with his attribute [of suppressing lust] as noted above,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא נִגְאֲלוּ עַל יְדֵי אֶחָד מִזַּרְעוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה טָעוּת דִּבְנֵי אֶפְרַיִם שֶׁיָּצְאוּ קֹדֶם זְמַנָּם;
nevertheless they were not redeemed through one of his descendants, as witnessed in the tragic error of the sons of Ephraim who departed prematurely;
וְהַגַּם דְּ"וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹמֵר" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן מֵאֶפְרַיִם "נַעַר לֹא יָמִישׁ מִתּוֹךְ הָאֹהֶל" [שְׁמוֹת ל״ג:י״א] וּמַכְנִיס לָאָרֶץ;
and although Moses took Joseph's bones as mentioned, and Joshua son of Nun from Ephraim ("a young man, departed not out of the Tent") brought them into the Land;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִקַּר גְּאֻלָּה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה שֶׁהוּא עֶצֶם מָשִׁיחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, וְאַהֲרֹן, שֶׁהֵם כֹּהֲנִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה גַּם עַל מֹשֶׁה;
nevertheless the primary redemption was executed through Moses—who is the essence of Mashiach, as written in Raya Mehemna—and Aaron, who are priests, as the Sages stated also regarding Moses;
כִּי עַל יְדֵי לְאַכְפַּיָּא לְבַד אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל הַנִּצּוּחַ גָּמוּר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "בֶּעָוֹן מָלֵא אֲפִילּוּ וְכוּלֵי", וְזֶהוּ עֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
for through suppression alone total victory is impossible, as our Sages noted: "In iniquity was I shapeless—even the most pious...", which is the venom of the serpent,
כִּי יִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת נִקְרָא אֲכִילָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "אָכְלָה וּמָחֲתָה פִיהָ", וְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִתְהַוָּה עַל יְדֵי הַזּוּהֲמָא דְּנָחָשׁ;
for the inclination for sexual transgression is termed eating ("she eats and wipes her mouth"), and the inclination for idolatry was generated through the serpent's contamination;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן, וְלֹא עָבְדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר עֲרָיוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין [ס״ג עַמּוּד ב׳];
and Israel having stood at Sinai shed that defilement, having served idols solely to permit forbidden relationships (Sanhedrin 63b);

וְאֵין אֶצְלָם רַק יִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ עֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ בַּאֲכִילָה, וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת? דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו";

leaving within them only the sexual drive, which is the root of the serpent's counsel in eating, prompting the retort: "Was the Torah given to ministering angels?", for "the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth";
וְאֵין עֵצָה כְּלָל בִּלְאַכְפַּיָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּאֶפְשָׁרוּת כֹּחַ אָדָם, רַק בִּלְאִתְהַפְּכָא עַל יְדֵי סֵפֶר תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֲכִילָה כְּמוֹ קָרְבָּנוֹת.

and there is no complete remedy through mere suppression, which exceeds human capacity, but rather through transformation (le-ithapcha) via the book of Torat Kohanim (Leviticus), sanctifying eating to be like holy sacrifices.

Through that eating the light became concealed from him, until it appeared to him that he had an existence of his own, with free choice. Beforeward he recognized with clarity that he was included in Hashem’s will. The repair of this eating is the eating of matzah. paragraphs.text: Shabbat 146a: “When the serpent came upon Chavah, it cast contamination into her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their contamination cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have it cease. The Gemara asks about converts and answers that although they themselves were not there, their spiritual root was there.”

p: אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם שֶׁיֹּאכַל כָּל מַעֲדַנֵּי עוֹלָם וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לֹא יֵהָנֶה מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלוּם, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי: "וְלֹא נֶהֱנֵיתִי בְּאֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה" [כְּתוּבוֹת ק״ד עַמּוּד א׳];

It is possible for a person to eat all the delicacies of the world and yet derive no worldly enjoyment whatsoever, in the manner Rebbe declared: "I did not enjoy even with my small finger" [Ketubot 104a];
וְהִקְשׁוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת מֵהָא דְּלֹא פָּסְקָה מֵעַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וּבֶאֱמֶת וַדַּאי הָיָה לוֹ שֻׁלְחַן מְלָכִים,
and Tosafot challenged this from the tradition that radish and lettuce never ceased from his table winter and summer, for he certainly maintained a royal table,
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרָה דְּ"לַה' הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ", שֶׁעַל זֶה הוּא הַבְּרָכָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כֵּיצַד מְבָרְכִין [בְּרָכוֹת ל״ה עַמּוּד א׳],
yet it was through recognizing that "the earth is Hashem's and the fullness thereof," which forms the basis of the blessing (Berakhot 35a),

הַיְינוּ שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵאֲמִתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ, הַטַּעַם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּמַּאֲכָל שֶׁנֶּעֱרָב לַחֵךְ, וְכֹחַ הַחִיּוּת שֶׁבּוֹ לְהַחֲיוֹת הַגּוּף, אֵינוֹ בַּמַּאֲכָל מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְנֶהֱנֶה מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;

meaning that he knows that everything stems from His true essence: the delicious taste pleasing to the palate and the sustaining energy within it do not belong to the food intrinsically—which would constitute worldly pleasure;
רַק הוּא כֹּחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ", וְהַכֹּל הוּא לַה', שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא הַמְמַלֵּא כָּל עָלְמִין, וְאָז נַעֲשָׂה מַאֲכָלוֹ דֻּגְמַת הַמָּן מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם;
but are the power of the Blessed Name, "there is none else beside Him," all belonging to the Tetragrammaton filling all worlds, whereupon his food becomes like the Manna from heaven;

כִּי "הַשָּׁמַיִם שָׁמַיִם לַה' וְהָאָרֶץ [נָתַן לִבְנֵי אָדָם]" וְגוֹמֵר [תְּהִלִּים קט״ו:ט״ז], וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא מַכִּיר בְּבִרְכָתוֹ דְּ"לַה' הָאָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר", הֲרֵי נַעֲשָׂה מֵאֶרֶץ שָׁמַיִם, וּמַאֲכָלוֹ לֶחֶם שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִין,

for "the heavens are the heavens of Hashem, but the earth He gave to the children of men," and when he acknowledges through his blessing that the earth is Hashem's, earth is transformed into heaven, his sustenance becoming bread that ministering angels eat,
שֶׁגַּם מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת יֵשׁ לָהֶם מָזוֹן, דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא קִיּוּם חִיּוּתָם, וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי חִיּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַשּׁוֹפֵעַ בָּהֶם;
for even ministering angels require sustenance sustaining their being, namely the divine vitality flowing within them;
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא אָמְרוּ בִּפְתִיחַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ [בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳]: אֵין בּוֹ לֹא אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּה וְכוּלֵי רַק נִזּוֹנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה;
and likewise in the World to Come (Berakhot 17a): there is neither eating nor drinking, but the righteous delight in the radiance of the Shechinah;
כִּי בְּלֹא מָזוֹן אִי אֶפְשָׁר, דְּכָךְ יִסֵּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִהְיוֹת כָּל נִבְרָא בַּעַל גְּבוּל צָרִיךְ לְמָזוֹן הַמְקַיֵּם כֹּחַ חִיּוּתוֹ,
for without sustenance existence is impossible, Hashem having established that every bounded creature requires nourishment sustaining its vital force,
רַק שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה מֻפְשָׁט מִלְּבוּשׁ, וְיִהְיֶה הַמָּזוֹן זִיו הַשְּׁכִינָה;
only that then it will be stripped of physical garments, the food being the radiance of the Shechinah;
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא בִּלְבוּשׁ, אֲבָל הַבְּרָכָה הוּא הַהַכָּרָה מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹךְ הַלְּבוּשׁ וּבִפְנִימִיּוּתוֹ.
while in this world it is clothed in matter, the blessing being the recognition of what lies within the garment and in its interior.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנָּחָשׁ "עָפָר לַחְמוֹ" בְּכָל מַעֲדַנֵּי עוֹלָם, וְטוֹעֵם טַעַם עָפָר שֶׁהוּא הַיּוֹתֵר תַּחְתּוֹן שֶׁבְּעוֹלַם עֲשִׂיָּה;
And just as the serpent's bread is dust amid all delicacies of the world, tasting only dust—the lowliest element of the world of Asiyah;

כָּךְ הַמֻּבְדָּל מִכֹּחַ הַנָּחָשׁ, רָצָה לוֹמַר כֹּחַ הַתַּאֲוָה (כְּמוֹ רַבִּי דְּלֹא מֵת, דֻּגְמַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כַּנּוֹדָע הוּא הָיָה נָקִי מֵעֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ לְגַמְרֵי),
so one detached from the serpent's power—meaning the force of lust (like Rebbe who did not die, mirroring Jacob our father, being completely pure of the serpent's counsel)—
גַּם שֶׁאוֹכֵל כָּל מַעֲדַנֵּי עוֹלָם אֵינוֹ טוֹעֵם אֶלָּא חִיּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמְלֻבָּשׁ בּוֹ.
even while eating all earthly delicacies tastes only the vitality of the Blessed Name clothed within it.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן "לֹא נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי הַמָּן" [תַּנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח כ׳], שֶׁכָּל מַאֲכָלָם הוּא דֻּגְמַת הַמָּן, לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מֵעֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, לָזֶה נִתְּנוּ כָּל רָזֵי תּוֹרָה;

And this is "The Torah was given only to the eaters of the Manna" [Tanchuma, Beshalach 20], for one whose food resembles the Manna—bread from heaven, free of the serpent's venom—is granted all mysteries of the Torah;
כִּי עַל יְדֵי עֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ נִתַּן כְּרוּבִים וְלַהַט הַחֶרֶב הַמִּתְהַפֶּכֶת לִשְׁמֹר אֶת דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים, וַעֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ הָיָה רַק בְּעִנְיַן הָאֲכִילָה בְּתַאֲוָה;
because through the serpent's counsel the cherubim and flaming turning sword were set to guard the way to the Tree of Life, the serpent's counsel existing entirely in lustful eating;

וְאוֹכְלֵי הַמָּן, הַיְינוּ בַּכַּוָּנָה הַנִּזְכֶּרֶת לְעֵיל וּמְתַקֵּן עֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ לְגַמְרֵי, נִסְתַּלְּקוּ הַשּׁוֹמְרִים מִדֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים אֶצְלוֹ, וְאֵין עֵץ הַחַיִּים אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה.
and for those eating like the Manna with the aforementioned intent, rectifying the serpent's venom, the guardians of the Tree of Life are removed, the Tree of Life being the Torah.
וּלְכָךְ רַבִּי הוּא שֶׁסִּדֵּר הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת שֶׁהוּא יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כְּמוֹ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
Therefore Rebbe compiled the Mishnah—the bedrock of the Oral Torah—just as Moses our teacher gave the Written Torah;

דַּהֲוָה מֵאוֹכְלֵי הַמָּן בְּפֹעַל מַמָּשׁ, נִגְלֶה לָעַיִן שֶׁהַלֶּחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, וּלְכָךְ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא מְפֹרָשׁ שֶׁהַלֶּחֶם הוּא מֵה' בֶּאֱמֶת, וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב דִּכְתִיבָא וּמַנָּחָא;
Moses experiencing the Manna visibly as bread from heaven, which is why the Written Torah openly declares that bread is truly from Hashem, lying open and explicit;
וְהָיָה קַיָּם זֶה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַנְּבוּאָה קַיֶּמֶת, דִּנְבוּאָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן דָּבָר מְפֹרָשׁ מֵה', וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִגְנְזָה צִנְצֶנֶת הַמָּן;
and this clarity endured as long as prophecy existed, prophecy being an explicit divine word, after which the jar of Manna was hidden away;
וְהַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן בָּזֶה בְּהֶעְלֵם, לְהָבִין בְּדַעְתּוֹ וּבְהַשְׂכָּלָתוֹ דָּבָר זֶה,
leaving the perception of divine sustenance concealed, to be grasped through intellectual discernment;
וְזֶהוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁנִּתְיַסְּדָה לִהְיוֹת כְּתִיבָא וּמַנָּחָא עַל יְדֵי רַבִּי, שֶׁהוּא בֵּרֵר דָּבָר זֶה גַּם בְּהֶעְלֵם, הַיְינוּ הַלֶּחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מֵה',
which is the Oral Torah codified in writing by Rebbe, who clarified even within concealment that bread from the earth originates exclusively from Hashem,
וְזֶה כָּל עִקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דְּהַיְינוּ חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, הוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and this is the foundational core of the Oral Torah: that the wisdom of Israel is likewise directly from the Blessed Name.
וְכֹחַ זֶה גָּדוֹל, שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע — עֵץ הַחַיִּים;
And this power is immense, transforming the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil into the Tree of Life;
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כֹּחוֹ מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים מַמָּשׁ, וְזֶה אָחַז בְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע וַעֲשָׂאוֹ עֵץ הַחַיִּים, וְהָבֵן זֶה.
for Moses drew his power directly from the Tree of Life, whereas Rebbe took hold of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil and elevated it into the Tree of Life; understand this.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ: כָּל הַשּׁוֹנֶה הֲלָכוֹת — רָצָה לוֹמַר מִשְׁנָיוֹת — מֻבְטָח שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא, דְּהַיְינוּ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם דְּעֵץ הַחַיִּים.
Therefore the Sages taught: "Whoever reviews Halakhot—meaning the Mishnah—is guaranteed a place in the World to Come," which is the eternal life of the Tree of Life.

paragraphs.text: Ketubot 104a:6: “At the time of Rebbe’s passing, he raised his ten fingers toward Heaven and said: Master of the world, it is revealed and known before You that I labored in Torah with my ten fingers and did not enjoy even with my little finger. May it be Your will that there be peace in my rest. A heavenly voice emerged and said: ‘He shall enter peace; they shall rest upon their beds.’”

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 11a:6:1-2: “Although we say that Rebbe did not enjoy this world even with his little finger, nevertheless many people ate at his table. The statement that radish never ceased from their table is significant because they served large meals and needed foods that cut through and turn over the food and broaden the intestines.”

paragraphs.text: Divrei Chalomot 5: “One who has tasted fear of sin and entered the paths of piety knows that its beginning is to sanctify one’s eating. The teaching to pray that excessive food and drink not enter one’s body means eating without holiness; rather, all should be in holiness, as with Rebbe. He was called our holy master because he did not enjoy this world, although the Gemara says that radish and lettuce never ceased from his table: everything was in holiness. Satisfaction from the desire for eating without holiness draws transgression after it: ‘Lest you eat and be sated ... and your heart grow proud and you forget.’ Thus ‘Guard yourselves’ applies to eating and satisfaction being in holiness, lest otherwise the heart be drawn away of itself.”

p: כַּאֲשֶׁר אֲכִילָתוֹ כָּרָאוּי, וְהַיְינוּ בִּידִיעָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּאֲכִיל, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ [וְאֶת מֵימֶיךָ] וַהֲסִרֹתִי [מַחֲלָה מִקִּרְבֶּךָ]" [שְׁמוֹת כ״ג:כ״ה],

When one's eating is conducted properly—with the conscious knowledge that the Blessed Name provides the nourishment—concerning this it is said: "And He shall bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst" [Exodus 23:25],
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּכֹחַ הַלֶּחֶם וְהַמַּיִם שֶׁאוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה לְהָסִיר כָּל מִינֵי מַחֲלָה;
that the bread and water consumed possess the inherent potency to banish all manner of disease;

כִּי דָּבָר שֶׁיִּסֵּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַחֲיוֹת נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם, הֲרֵי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ חִיּוּת גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וַדַּאי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ לְקַיֵּם חִיּוּתוֹ לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרָעוּ שׁוּם מַחֲלָה;
for a substance established by the Blessed Name to sustain human life contains divine vitality, certainly possessing the capacity to preserve health entirely without illness befalling him;
וְכֵן יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַקִּיּוּם לְעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרָעוּ הַמָּוֶת כְּלָל,
and it likewise possesses the power of eternal preservation, preventing death from occurring at all,
כִּי כֹּחַ הַמַּאֲכָל הוּא לְהַחֲזִיק חִיּוּתוֹ בּוֹ כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם,
for the true nature of food is to maintain vitality forever,

רַק עַל יְדֵי חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בַּמַּאֲכָל נִגְזְרָה הַמִּיתָה, דְּהַיְינוּ קִלְקוּל כֹּחַ קִיּוּם הַחִיּוּת שֶׁבַּמַּאֲכָל, שֶׁבַּדָּבָר שֶׁקִּלְקֵל בּוֹ נֶעֱנַשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בַּמַּאֲכָל כֹּחַ כָּל כָּךְ.

and only through the sin of Adam involving food was death decreed, which corrupted the sustaining power within food, punishing him in the very medium through which he sinned by weakening its life-giving force.

וּמַצָּה נִקְרָא "מֵיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָתָא", וַדַּאי הוּא רְפוּאָה לְמַכָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "מַחַץ מַכָּתוֹ יִרְפָּא" [יְשַׁעְיָהוּ ל׳:כ״ו], דְּזֶהוּ סְתָם רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה שֶׁבַּכָּתוּב

And matzah is called "the food of healing," certainly serving as the cure for the primeval wound of the world, as our Sages expounded on "and heals the stroke of their wound" [Isaiah 30:26], which is the quintessential healing in Scripture

(וְזֶה טַעַם "כִּי אֲנִי ה' רֹפְאֶךָ", שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אִם אֵין מַכָּה רְפוּאָה לָמָּה? רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר: לְמַכָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָרוֹפֵא, וּמִמֵּילָא "כָּל הַמַּחֲלָה וְגוֹמֵר", דִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא רְפוּאַת מַכָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, אִם כֵּן מִסְּתָמָא מַכּוֹת דְּמִצְרַיִם הָיָה לְפִי שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד זֶה);

(and this resolves the question on "for I am Hashem that heals you": Hashem is the healer of the cosmic wound of creation, and since the Exodus prepared for the Torah which heals that wound, Egypt's plagues punished their opposition to it);

וְהַיְינוּ לְכֹחַ הָאֲכִילָה; רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ מִיתָה מִצַּד עֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ — פֵּרוּשׁ, הוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: שֶׁבָּא נָחָשׁ וְהִטִּיל זוּהֲמָא, וְאוֹתָהּ זוּהֲמָא הַיְינוּ בְּתַאֲוַת זִמָּה,
and this cures the faculty of eating; yet mortality still lingers through the counsel of the serpent, referring to the defilement injected into Eve by the serpent, which resides in sexual lust,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: אֲפִילּוּ חֲסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בּוֹ צַד נִדְנוּד רַע, שֶׁהוּא מֵאַרְבָּעָה שֶׁמֵּתוּ בַּעֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ [שַׁבָּת נ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳];
concerning which the Sages stated that even the most pious cannot escape a subtle trace of this flaw, as seen in the four who died solely through the counsel of the serpent [Shabbat 55b];
רַק יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן, וְאָז הָיוּ בֶּאֱמֶת חֵרוּת מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּמִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת לוּלֵי הַחֵטְא אַחַר כָּךְ;
yet when Israel stood at Sinai their defilement ceased, granting them true freedom from the evil inclination and death, had they not sinned later with the Golden Calf;
וִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הוּא הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, לְכָךְ מִקֹּדֶם אֲכִילַת מַצָּה לְרַפְּאוֹת חֵטְא דַּאֲכִילָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא הֲסָרַת הַזּוּהֲמָא,
and the Exodus being preparation for Sinai, eating matzah comes first to cure the sin of eating, so that one may subsequently reach the Giving of the Torah to purge sexual defilement,
דְּזֶהוּ סְתָם יֵצֶר בְּדִבְרֵי חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם, כְּמוֹ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק: יֵצֶר תִּינוֹק וְכוּלֵי וּבִשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת;
which is the standard meaning of "inclination" throughout rabbinic literature (as in Sanhedrin 107b: the inclination, a child, and a wife, etc.);

וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע, בָּרָאתִי תוֹרָה תַּבְלִין" [קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳], וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ מְנֻוָּל וְכוּלֵי" [סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳], דְּיֵצֶר דִּזְנוּת נִקְרָא "מְנֻוָּל", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "אִשָּׁה חֲמַת מָלֵא וְכוּלֵי", וְאֵין נִוּוּל גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה, וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא זֶה זוּהֲמָא שֶׁהוּא זִהוּם וּמֵאוּס;

and on this they stated: "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as an antidote-spice," and "If this repulsive one encounters you...", lust being termed repulsive (Shabbat 152a), an abhorrent contamination;

וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַהַצָּלָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְדַוְקָא כְּשֶׁקָּדַם אֲכִילַת מַצָּה דְּלֵיל פֶּסַח לְרַפְּאוֹת תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם נִמְשָׁכִים זֶה מִזֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מְלֵי כְּרֵיסֵיהּ זַנֵּי בִּישֵׁי" [בְּרָכוֹת ל״ב עַמּוּד א׳];

and deliverance from this is achieved through Torah study, specifically when preceded by eating matzah on Seder night to heal appetite first, since gluttony leads directly to promiscuity (Berakhot 32a);

וְעַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת חַוָּה מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת גָּרַם בִּיאַת נָחָשׁ עָלֶיהָ אַחַר כָּךְ, וְזֶה הָיָה עֲטָיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וַעֲצָתוֹ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כִּשְׁלוֹנָהּ בְּתַאֲוַת אֲכִילָה יוּכַל לָהּ בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן;
Eve's eating from the Tree of Knowledge causing the serpent to cohabit with her, the serpent scheming that by causing her to stumble in eating he would master her in lust;

וְכֵן בְּהֵיפֶךְ: עַל יְדֵי מַצָּה הַנּוֹתֶנֶת קְדוּשָׁה בָּאֲכִילָה, יִזְכֶּה גַּם כֵּן לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה דְּגֶדֶר עֶרְוָה, דְּמִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרֻבָּה, וַאֲכִילַת מִצְוָה כָּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁגּוֹרֶרֶת קְדוּשָׁה בַּעֲרָיוֹת עַל אַחַת חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּמַכּוֹת [כ״ג עַמּוּד א׳].
and conversely: through matzah instilling holiness into eating, one merits Torah in the sanctity of sexual purity, the measure of goodness being five hundred times greater (Makkot 23a).

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Av 4:2: “The letter tet signifies life. The month’s repair is that the angel of death should no longer rule, and this is possible only when all the serpent’s damage is repaired, whose beginning was enjoyment of eating. Therefore the Sefer Yetzirah associates the letter with eating: the eating itself is to be in holiness. This is especially so when Rosh Chodesh Av falls on Shabbat. The central point is to delight the additional soul for the sake of Heaven, yet bodily enjoyment, too, is in holiness. Shabbat is the time to repair eating so that it is in holiness, from the side of the Tree of Life: those who taste it merit life.”

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 32a:8-13: “The school of Rabbi Yannai said: A lion does not roar over a basket of straw, but over a basket of meat. Rav Acha son of Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Sheshet: This is what people say: A full belly produces bad sorts. For it is said, ‘As they grazed they became sated; they were sated and their heart grew proud; therefore they forgot Me.’ Rav Nachman said: The source is, ‘Your heart will grow proud, and you will forget Hashem.’ The Sages said: It is, ‘He will eat, become sated and fat, and turn away.’”

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Makkot 23a:20:1: “The measure of goodness is greater than the measure of punishment by five hundred. Concerning punishment it says, ‘Visiting the fathers’ iniquity upon children to the third and fourth generations’; concerning goodness it says, ‘Doing kindness to thousands,’ translated as thousands of generations. Four generations against two thousand generations gives one to five hundred; the minimum of ‘thousands’ is two thousand, and all the more if the expression is taken to mean thousands to the end of all generations.”
